Fiordland installs on Btrfs and takes automatic snapshots with [https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Snapper snapper]. A snapshot is a frozen copy of the system (not your home folder) at a point in time.

== When snapshots are taken ==
* Before and after every package install, removal or update (snap-pac).
* Every hour, kept as: 5 hourly, 7 daily, 2 weekly, 1 monthly.

List them:
<pre>snapper -c root list</pre>

== Undo a change while the system still boots ==
Find the "pre" snapshot number from before the bad update, then:
<pre>sudo snapper -c root undochange PRE..POST</pre>
Reboot afterwards.

== Roll back when the system does not boot ==
# Restart. In the boot menu, open '''Fiordland snapshots''' and pick one from before the problem. Each entry shows the date and what caused it (for example <code>pacman -Syu</code>).
# The system starts from that snapshot. Changes made now are kept in memory only and are lost at the next restart.
# If it works, make it permanent:
#: <code>sudo fiordland-rollback</code>
# Restart. Fiordland now starts from the restored system.
# Once everything works, free the space used by the old system: <code>sudo fiordland-rollback --clean</code>

Each snapshot includes its own kernel, so rolling back also undoes a bad kernel update. Your home folder is never touched.

To restore a snapshot without booting it first, use its number from <code>fiordland-rollback --list</code>:
<pre>sudo fiordland-rollback 42</pre>

== Installs from before 23 November 2026 ==
Older installs use systemd-boot and keep the kernel on the boot partition, so the snapshot menu is not available. Use the steps below instead.

# Boot the Fiordland USB stick and open a terminal.
# Find your Fiordland partition: <code>lsblk -f</code> (the Btrfs one, for example <code>/dev/nvme0n1p2</code>).
# Mount the top of the filesystem:
#: <code>sudo mount -o subvolid=5 /dev/nvme0n1p2 /mnt</code>
# Pick a snapshot: <code>sudo ls /mnt/@snapshots</code> and check <code>sudo cat /mnt/@snapshots/N/info.xml</code> for its date.
# Move the broken system aside and restore the snapshot:
#: <code>sudo mv /mnt/@ /mnt/@broken</code>
#: <code>sudo btrfs subvolume snapshot /mnt/@snapshots/N/snapshot /mnt/@</code>
# <code>sudo umount /mnt</code> and reboot.
# If a kernel update caused the problem, reinstall the kernels: <code>sudo pacman -S linux-cachyos linux</code>.
